text:
meera: FYI customer Shoply (priority: high) reporting a bunch of 504s and long tail p99s since ~09:10 UTC. Alerts firing: ingress_queue_depth > 95% + continuous-batcher backlog climbing. forwarding traces and a short repro from support ticket #INC-4821.

support-bot: Ticket INC-4821 created and linked to customer. alert: ingress_queue_depth_high (firing). :rotating_light:

riley: looking. can someone paste the repo query for queue depth and continuous-batcher backlog? want raw numbers.

sam: PromQL I'm watching:
```
max_over_time(redis_queue_depth{service="ingress"}[5m])
sum(rate(continuous_batcher_backlog_total[1m])) by (cluster)
```
Right now queue_depth = 1832 (limit=2000), backlog rate jumped to ~420/min

carla: logs show lots of `batch_wait_ms` > window and `kv_cache_miss` spikes around same time. suspect KV cache eviction / memory pressure.

alex: can confirm KV cache eviction count spiked at 09:08 UTC. mem.used% on kvcache hosts hit 92% and eviction_rate surged. when kvcache misses, requests block getting KV keys -> longer batch latencies -> queue pileup.

dan: repro steps from support (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-v1","input":"'$(yes "lorem" | head -n 200 | tr '\n' ' ')'"}'
```
They send many short requests that keep active KV prefixes and then a small fraction of heavy prompts triggering long KV lookups.

meera: customer impact: ~30% of requests get 504, p99 token-latency up from 1.2s -> 12s. they say retries are causing billing spikes. support asked for short mitigation plan.

riley: short mitigations:
- throttle tenant at ingress (soft reject 429 at 70% queue) -> cheap immediate relief
- temporary routing to fallback model `rwd-small-v1` for that tenant
- bump `max_queue_depth` on hosted gateway (but careful, this increases memory usage)
- reduce `max_batching_window_ms` from 50 -> 10 to flush batches faster

sam: Quick check: lowering batch window will increase per-token cost but reduces tail latency. I can push a canary config to 1 host group.

carla: also enabling `prefetch_kvcache=true` for the tenant could reduce misses on hot prefixes (pre-populate). requires a small runtime flag flip.

alex: I can increase kvcache capacity on the affected shard and raise eviction threshold from 85% -> 92% temporarily. will monitor.

dan: I'll run the repro locally against the canary after config changes and paste logs.

support-bot: Customer notified of mitigation plan: throttle + fallback + infra tweaks. ETA to customer: 20m. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Pager duty note: oncall riley assigned. runbook: `ingress-queue-surge` linked.

riley: started throttle for tenant `shoply` -> applied 70% soft-reject rule. watch queue depth.

sam: deployed canary with `max_batching_window_ms=10` to two hosts in us-west-2 using `infra rollout canary --group=batchers-usw2 --config batch_window=10` — no regressions so far.

alex: bumped kvcache memory on shard kvc-7 and raised eviction threshold. eviction_rate dropping in the last 3m.

dan: repro against canary shows p99 improved from 12s -> 1.8s in canary hosts. sample log snippet:
```
[09:34:11] request_id=xxxx batch_wait_ms=7 kv_cache_miss=false model_latency_ms=180
```

meera: support confirmed customer saw a drop in 504s after mitigation. they're still asking for a long-term fix and explanation for root cause.

carla: root cause summary draft:
- KV cache memory spikes caused evictions -> increased KV misses
- Misses cause longer continuous-batcher execution paths (hot prefixes needed) -> batch processing slows -> ingress queue depth climbs and hits queue depth guardrails -> tail 504s for waiting requests

riley: next steps (action items):
- engineering: add better kvcache telemetry per-tenant + hot-prefix heatmap (owner: alex)
- infra: increase default kvcache capacity and tune eviction policy (owner: alex)
- runtime: make `max_batching_window_ms` adaptive based on real-time queue depth (owner: sam)
- product: follow up with Shoply on throttling impact and bill adjustments (owner: meera/support)

meera: creating follow-up ticket ENG-9234 with the mitigation notes and action items. CC: support, infra, runtime.

support-bot: ENG-9234 linked to INC-4821 and assigned to engineering triage.

sam: re-open if we see queue depth creeping back after hosts warm up. will leave canary config for 30m then roll if stable.

riley: closing incident thread for now. keep monitoring dashboards and post any anomalies here. :lock:
